description: Canonical normalized scent-trait vocabulary for FragranceFinder recommendation data. Categories are descriptive organization only and are not recommendation-scoring rules.

traits.description: Amber-like warmth, resinous sweetness or glowing warmth.
Watery, marine, rain, spring-water or sea-air character.
Berry-focused fruit character such as raspberry or strawberry.
Citrus character such as bergamot, orange, tangerine or lemon.
Recognizable coconut character.
Cooling or chilling sensory impression.
Creamy, whipped, milky, buttery or soft lactonic impression.
Recognizable flower or floral-bouquet character.
General crisp or refreshing impression when a more specific fresh trait does not fully describe it.
General fruit character not fully represented by a more specific fruit trait.
Edible, dessert, bakery or food-like fragrance character.
Herbal or aromatic plant character.
Recognizable mint or spearmint character.
Musky, skin-like or soft musk character.
Recognizable patchouli character.
Powdery, cosmetic or soft vintage-style texture.
Effervescent, bubbly, fizzy or sparkling impression.
General perceived sweetness.
Recognizable vanilla character.
General warm, cozy or heated fragrance impression.
Wood character such as sandalwood, mahogany, teakwood or driftwood.
Leafy, dewy, grassy, aloe-like or fresh-green plant character.
Laundry-clean, linen-clean, freshly washed or detergent-like character.
Recognizable spice character such as clove, cinnamon or pumpkin spice.
Recognizable nutty character such as pistachio or pecan-like nuances.
Coffee, espresso, latte or roasted-coffee character.
Whiskey, rum, liqueur, spirit or distinctly boozy fragrance character.
Recognizable tea character that should not automatically be treated as generic Fresh or Herbal.
Recognizable apple character.
Earthy, mossy, vetiver-like or grounded forest-floor character.
Light, airy, breezy or spacious impression distinct from generic freshness.
Tart, tangy or mouth-puckering fruit brightness.
